page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage-focused virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is a key feature, offering 11519 GB of capacity with Premium Storage capability, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU metrics, database operations, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range. However, a notable performance tradeoff exists in memory bandwidth; while cached small-block reads are average, uncached large-block read memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given the high local storage capacity of over 11 TB and a balanced 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is configured for data-intensive workloads. It is suitable for hosting databases, executing large-scale text processing, and running local file-serving operations. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy machine learning training, though it achieves strong text generation speeds on small language models. The high resource density of local storage relative to the compute allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy deployments that do not require massive multi-core scaling.

It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 11519 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, with the latter ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core compute, database operations, and cached memory bandwidth perform at average levels, though uncached large-block read memory bandwidth represents a performance tradeoff, ranking in the bottom 25%. Lacking a GPU, this server is optimized for storage-heavy and memory-intensive applications. It is suitable for database hosting, text processing, and local file serving, offering high storage density relative to its compute resources.
